text:
maria: alert — apiserver p99 latency jumped ~11:45 UTC, many kubelets on gpu-pool started failing readiness probes
leo: saw that, dashboards show apiserver_request_duration_seconds p99 ~1.2s and spike in watch events backlog
aj: oncall ping (I'm OOO for 30m), but can help from phone
sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-145, paging oncall team :rotating_light:
maria: quick facts: controller-manager leader flips twice, a few nodes in gpu-pool got Rebooted by cloud provider at same window, lots of pod evictions around 11:43
ophelia: rolling window looks like kubelet eviction pressure triggered because nodefs/pressure + high memory usage from model-serving pods (batch jobs)
leo: suspect: autoscaler attempted scale-down during high load -> kubelet started evicting best-effort pods -> lots of watch/churn hitting apiserver -> apiserver CPU spike -> request latency -> controller-manager timeouts -> leader election jitter
maria: example kubelet log snippet:
```
Mar 15 11:43:12 kubelet[1234]: eviction manager: attempt to reclaim resource nodefs. Reclaimed 0 bytes
Mar 15 11:43:15 kubelet[1234]: Evicting pod "batch-transform-9" (memory pressure)
```
aj: can we confirm whether the autoscaler used the GPU-backed node groups for scale-down? if yes we should disable scale-down until we patch thresholds
ophelia: yes autoscaler config for gpu-pool has aggressive scale-down (utilization threshold 0.2, empty after 5m). That seems too aggressive during bursty training traffic
leo: also noticed kube-apiserver flags: --max-requests-inflight=400, we hit connection spikes. Might temporary increase to 800 to absorb fanout while we stabilize
maria: cost tradeoff: increasing inflight and keeping buffer means more headroom but higher memory/cpu on apiserver pods and cost of upscaling control plane in prod replicas
aj: quick mitigation steps I can trigger remotely: 1) suspend cluster-autoscaler scale-down for gpu-pool, 2) cordon a couple of low-util compute-only nodes to reduce eviction churn, 3) increase apiserver max-inflight to 800 and restart apiserver pods one at a time
sre-bot: deploy-bot: rolling restart requested for kube-apiserver (1/3) by aj
ophelia: also propose changing kubelet eviction threshold for available memory on gpu nodes from 100Mi to 50Mi and bump gracePeriod for readinessProbe to reduce flapping
leo: ops question — do we have prefix/KV cache pressure metrics? if K/V cache misses spiking, watch events amplify.
maria: kvcache_miss_rate did spike ~5x during the window, matching leader flips. might be due to node churn with large number of pods (model shards)
aj: executing step 1 now — suspended scale-down on gpu-pool (tainted note: temp flag set)
maria: monitoring — latency trending down but still above baseline, controller-manager leader still unstable
leo: running quick kubectl to list pods in kube-system for restarts:
```
kubectl get pods -n kube-system -o wide | egrep "apiserver|controller-manager|cloud-controller"
apiserver-0   1/1   Running   2 (10m ago)   10.0.0.5
apiserver-1   1/1   Running   1 (50m ago)   10.0.0.6
controller-manager-0  1/1 Running 3 (7m ago) 10.0.0.7
```
ophelia: looks like apiserver-0 restarted during spike, apiserver-1 stable, controller-manager flapped a few times
leo: If we suspect autoscaler + aggressive eviction, long-term fix: tune CA scaling policy for gpu-pool, add burst buffer (min nodes), and surface scheduling priority for model-serving pods so they avoid eviction class 'best-effort'
maria: also add a safety: make controller-manager pod anti-affinity to avoid leader churn if apiserver pod restarts coincide with node reboots
aj: all mitigations applied. will leave scale-down suspended for 2h and monitor. happy to revert earlier if stable
maria: thanks. follow-ups: create a playbook entry for "gpu-pool scale-down during burst" and propose new autoscaler config in next infra-ops sync
ophelia: I'll open a PR with suggested CA config and kubelet eviction tweak; will include simulated load test results
leo: thumbs up — if latency drops below 300ms for 15m we can close the incident and re-evaluate scale-down
sre-bot: Incident INC-2026-145 updated: status=monitoring
maria: noted — adding cost note: keeping extra gpu nodes for buffer ~+12% monthly spend, put in PR for budget approval
aj: any objections to keeping it for 24h?
leo: fine with 24h while we run tests
maria: closing update: latency trending steady, controller-manager leader stable for 9m, we'll re-evaluate in 1h
